html:
The Licchavis were the kings of the Kathmandu valley in Nepal from about 400 to 750, the first rulers of the valley known from their own inscriptions.

The oldest dated one, at the temple of Changu Narayan, was set up by King Manadeva I in 464. The kings were Hindu but gave land to Buddhist monasteries too, a mix that still marks the valley. Their trade linked India with Tibet, and Chinese envoys of the Tang dynasty described their palaces. Tradition says a Licchavi princess, Bhrikuti, married the Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo.

Shrines such as Swayambhunath and Pashupatinath grew in their time. After them the valley passed through obscure centuries until the Malla kings.
sum: The Licchavis were the kings of the Kathmandu valley in Nepal from about 400 to 750, the first rulers of the valley known from their own inscriptions.
